subject.title: Foreground reply fence (automatic mode) cancels delivery of completed replies to earlier concurrent group messages — reply shown in dashboard, never delivered to WhatsApp

question: Should a visible reply to one group message be allowed to suppress a completed reply to a different inbound message in the same group session, or should group-chat fence identity be per inbound message while direct-chat target freshness remains unchanged?
rationale: The production recurrence proves that sender-only isolation is insufficient, while the existing target-level fence was intentionally introduced to prevent stale replies. Selecting the permanent group supersession contract changes observable delivery semantics and cannot be inferred safely from a bounded-wait fix.

options.title: Use group per-message fences
options.body: Recommended: isolate group-chat replies by inbound-message identity, retain the current direct-chat target-level freshness rule, and add cancellation telemetry plus cross-channel regression tests.

options.title: Retain target-level freshness
options.body: Keep the current shared group-target fence only if maintainers explicitly accept that a newer visible group reply may suppress an earlier completed answer.

options.title: Design a richer supersession model
options.body: Define an explicit same-thread or explicit-replacement relation before changing the fence, accepting a larger design and validation effort.

recommendation.title: Use group per-message fences
recommendation.body: Recommended: isolate group-chat replies by inbound-message identity, retain the current direct-chat target-level freshness rule, and add cancellation telemetry plus cross-channel regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged foreground-fence work introduced the visibility-aware same-target contract whose intended boundary now requires clarification.
